# Cross-Repo & CI Ordering Checklist: Comprehensive live QuickFIX interop conversation

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the clauses spanning the two repositories — digest pinning, republish ordering, consumer blast radius, and the capability handshake (FR-016a/b/c, FR-026, R-11).
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [research.md](../research.md) §R-11 · [plan.md](../plan.md) §External obligations

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

> ⚠️ **This domain produced two defects that survived ten Gate A rounds**, both of the same shape: an
> obligation stated in one artifact and unreachable from the artifact a reader would consult. R-11
> decided *"pin `interop-smoke.yml` **and the existing cells**"*; the obligations table recorded only the
> first half, and the file carrying the second half had no row at all. These items test for more of it.

## Digest Pinning & Republish Ordering

- [x] CHK006 Is the ordering requirement — pin existing consumers **before** republishing — stated as a precondition rather than as a step that can be reordered? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026] — PASS: `plan.md` § *Structure Decision* consequence 4 (530-537, *"Step 0 of the ordering is therefore to pin..."*) and `tasks.md` T104's execution order (*"pin both consumers → merge → read digest → repoint cells"*) both commit unambiguously to pin-before-republish as the operative sequence for this feature. `spec.md` FR-026's *"Either ... or ..."* states the accepted solution space; the plan/tasks bind one path within it — not a contradiction. Non-PASS: plan.md/tasks.md leaving both orderings live, letting an implementer pick either at execution time.
- [x] CHK007 Are **all** consumers of the counterparty image enumerated in the requirements, with the enumeration method given so a new consumer is caught? [Completeness, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `plan.md`:638(d)** — the count is replaced by a **recipe with a discriminator**: *"DO NOT COUNT THE CONSUMERS — RE-DERIVE THEM: `grep -rln \"fixpp-interop-counterparties\" .github/workflows/ research/G19-fix-fpml-iso20022/library/.github/workflows/`"*, plus the discriminator the recipe needs and would otherwise mislead without — *a consumer resolves the image at run time while `publish-counterparties.yml` **creates** it*, so the publisher appears in that output and is not a consumer. ⚠️ **Verified by running it**: it returns three files, two consumers and the publisher — which is exactly why the discriminator is stated rather than left to the reader. `tasks.md`:62 (T003) is changed from *"Pin **both** … consumers"* to *"Pin **every** … consumer"* pointing at the recipe, so the hard-coded count is gone from the task too.
- [x] CHK008 Do the requirements account for consumers triggered on `pull_request` across all branches, where a pin merged to the default branch **does not reach open PRs**? [Edge Case, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `spec.md`:1004 (FR-026), stated as a CONDITION and not a file list** — *"Any consumer that resolves the counterparty image at run time under a `pull_request` trigger carrying `branches: [\"**\"]` is not reachable by a pin merged only to the default branch"*, with the mechanism given (that trigger admits PRs based on *any* branch, and such a run resolves its `IMAGE:` reference in its own base's context). ⚠️ **It also corrects FR-026's own *"the first is the safer shape"***, which was incomplete: pin-first is **inert for the default branch — which is what makes it safer there — and NOT inert for work already in flight**. ⚠️ Verified directly against both files before writing: `library/.github/workflows/interop-smoke.yml`:22-25 and the parent's `.github/workflows/interop-matrix.yml`:6-9 carry the identical trigger. Both obligation rows (`plan.md`:637, :638) repeat the *condition*, not the pair of filenames, so it does not re-arm when a third consumer appears.
- [x] CHK009 Is the tension between pinning the matrix to the pre-089 digest and 089's own cells needing the **new** image stated and resolved, rather than left for an implementer to discover? [Conflict, Spec §FR-016b] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `plan.md`:638(b)** — the tension is now **resolved in the bundle**, not deferred: *"AND THE TENSION THE PIN CREATES IS RESOLVED IN THE SAME CHANGE, NOT AT EXECUTION TIME"*, stating that a workflow-level pre-089 pin starves 089's own cells, that the override mechanism settled by `tasks.md` T004 lands **here as an obligation**, and — closing the shape the item objected to — that *"decide the mechanism"* left standing in a task is scored **ABSENT** under `plan.md`'s own round-2 acceptance rule. Both halves the item requires now hold.
- [x] CHK010 Are requirements defined for reading the published digest from the run's **step log** rather than the job conclusion? [Clarity, Gap] — PASS: `tasks.md` T104 states it with the failure it prevents — *"read the new digest from the publish run's **step log**, never `.conclusion`"* — consistent with this repo's own standing lesson that a green job conclusion is not evidence a step log carries a value. Non-PASS: no site in the bundle stating this, leaving an implementer to read `.conclusion` and get a plausible-looking value.
- [x] CHK011 Is the requirement that the image be referenced by **immutable digest, not a mutable tag** stated with the failure it prevents? [Traceability, Spec §FR-016b] — PASS: `spec.md` FR-016b (843-844) states the requirement together with the failure it prevents verbatim — *"so that the exact counterparty build behind any result is recoverable after the fact."* Non-PASS: the MUST-clause present with no stated consequence.
- [x] CHK012 Are the two acceptable orderings (pin-first vs publish-under-a-new-tag) both specified, with the trade-off stated, so a reader knows which was chosen and why? [Completeness, Research §R-11] — PASS: `spec.md` FR-026 (958-969) states both orderings explicitly with the trade-off (*"The first is the safer shape ... the alternative ... leaves a window in which `:latest` and the pinned digest disagree"*, `research.md` R-11 535-538); `plan.md`/`tasks.md` make clear the first was chosen (see CHK006). Non-PASS: only one ordering mentioned, or both mentioned with no stated trade-off/decision.

## Failure Direction of the Consumers

- [x] CHK013 Are requirements defined for the case where the image cannot be pulled — specifically that the consumer **skips with a reason and stays GREEN** — so that "089 is passing" is not read as "the cell ran"? [Coverage, Gap] — PASS: `spec.md`:367-369 (*"A skip must never satisfy a fidelity assertion, and the new evidence rows must record a skip as a skip"*) and FR-016 (838-839, *"A counterparty-unavailable outcome MUST remain distinguishable from a pass in both the cell result and the evidence record"*) state this directly. Non-PASS: no requirement distinguishing skip from pass, leaving "089 is passing" ambiguous with "the cell ran."
- [x] CHK014 Is the rule that an **unpullable pin is a skip, and a skip is green** stated at every site that pins a digest? [Consistency, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `spec.md`:845 (FR-016b — the digest-pin requirement itself) and at both obligation rows, `plan.md`:637 and :638(c)** — i.e. at every site that pins a digest, which is what the item asked for. FR-016b now reads *"AN UNPULLABLE PIN IS A SKIP, AND A SKIP IS GREEN"* with the anti-vacuity question spelled out — *ask what ELSE satisfies "the pinned cell passed": the cell not having run* — and each row repeats the failure direction for its own workflow rather than pointing away from itself.
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements specified for evidencing that a cell **actually ran**, as distinct from the job reporting success? [Measurability, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `spec.md`:845 (FR-016b) and `plan.md`:637 / :638(c)** — the *actually-ran* obligation is lifted out of `tasks.md` T104 and stated normatively for the pre-existing consumer cells this domain concerns: *"every site that pins a digest MUST also evidence that the cell **actually executed**, read from that run's own **step log** and never from the job conclusion."* Each of the two rows carries it for its own workflow. This does not extend FR-014's Level-1 population to those cells — it states the weaker, correct obligation for them, which is that a green check is not evidence the cell ran.
- [x] CHK016 Is a counterparty-unavailable outcome required to remain distinguishable from a pass in **both** the cell result and the evidence record? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016] — PASS: `spec.md` FR-016 (838-839) is a verbatim match. Non-PASS: the requirement silent on one of the two locations (cell result or evidence record).

## Capability Handshake

- [x] CHK017 Is the capability-minimums artifact identified as the single normative home of every required-version operand, with all pointing sites deferring to it rather than restating values? [Consistency, Plan §External obligations] — PASS: `plan.md`'s capability-minimums row (623, *"ONE ARTIFACT, AND EVERY COMPARISON RESOLVES ITS MINIMUM FROM IT ... NO CONSUMER ROSTER IS KEPT HERE"*) plus `contracts/readback-jsonl.md` C-2 (280) and C-12 (289) both point at the artifact rather than restating a value. Non-PASS: a version value duplicated at a second site — the exact hazard class this bundle's own retrospective (plan.md round 8) names as having produced four wrong compiler-diagnostic literals elsewhere.
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for a cell whose minimum is **not declared** — specifically that it FAILS rather than passing or skipping? [Edge Case, Contract §C-2] — PASS: `plan.md`'s capability-minimums row states it explicitly (*"a missing or unparseable artifact, a cell with no entry, or an entry omitting a capability the `hello` carries MUST FAIL the cell — never default to 'no minimum', never skip, never pass"*); `contracts/readback-jsonl.md` C-2/C-12 repeat the rule at the consumption site. Non-PASS: the undeclared-minimum case left to default silently to "no comparison performed."
- [x] CHK019 Is the pre-conversation hello gate specified to run **before** the gtest is launched, with the consequence of running it later stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016a] — PASS: `data-model.md`:150-153 and `research.md` R-4a part 2 (279-282) state the gate runs shim-side, before the gtest, with the consequence of running it later (the `unavailable:`/`skip:` collapse) stated at the same sites and again at `spec.md` FR-024's warning (936-940). Non-PASS: the ordering stated with no consequence, leaving an implementer free to move the check gtest-side.
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for an absent hello as a **failure** rather than a stale-peer skip, and is the distinction between "is it the right peer" and "is there a peer" drawn? [Ambiguity, Data-model §1] — PASS: `data-model.md`:136-139 draws the distinction verbatim (*"is a peer listening"* → skip vs. *"is it the right peer"* → failure), explicitly warning against collapsing them. Non-PASS: only the failure rule stated, with no contrast against the pre-existing availability-probe skip path.
- [x] CHK021 Is the requirement that `script_digest` be **recomputed** by each side over the file it actually opened — never copied from the environment — stated with the reason? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008c] — PASS: `data-model.md`:84-90, 112-115 state the recompute-not-copy rule with its reason (*"A verbatim copy would prove only that the counterparty can echo a string"*) for both the counterparty and fixpp sides. `spec.md` FR-008c itself states only the content-addressing requirement — the recompute/reason detail lives in data-model.md, the normal FR→data-model division this bundle uses throughout. Non-PASS: the rule stated as a bare MUST with no reason, or contradicted between the two sides.

## Two-Repository Boundary

- [x] CHK022 Is the split between parent-side counterparty *programs* and submodule-side *assertions* stated as a constraint with its reason (QuickFIX is deliberately outside fixpp's dependency graph)? [Clarity, Plan §Structure Decision] — PASS: `plan.md`:506-508, verbatim match including the reason (*"the counterparties link QuickFIX, which is deliberately outside fixpp's dependency graph"*). Non-PASS: the split stated with no reason, leaving a reader to guess why it's not negotiable.
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements defined for how parent-side C++/Java changes receive a review disposition, given that Gate A/B operate on the library PR? [Gap, Plan §Structure Decision] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `plan.md`:513 (§ *Structure Decision*, consequence 1) with its producer at `plan.md`:647** — the item's exact gap was a stated need with no mechanism, so a mechanism is named: the `/gate-b` brief for this feature **names the parent-side counterparty diff as in-scope**, enumerated at the head under review with `git -C <parent repo> diff --stat <merge-base>..HEAD -- phase-9-harness/ .github/workflows/` (⛔ re-derived at review time, never a file list written into the plan), and the reviewer's disposition is **recorded in this feature's Gate B record** — which gets its own § *External obligations* row under RC-B, since the record is outside the bundle. ⛔ *"Silence is not a disposition"* is stated at both sites: a gate record that never mentions the parent-side diff records that nobody looked.
- [x] CHK024 Is the consequence of a library PR merging **ahead** of the image specified as a broken tree, rather than left implicit in the ordering? [Coverage, Plan §Structure Decision] — PASS: `plan.md`:515-516, verbatim (*"A library PR merged ahead of the image is a broken tree"*). Non-PASS: the ordering stated with the failure mode left implicit.
- [x] CHK025 Are the requirements about what the publish **does not** cover — that the arm's verdict lands post-merge and gates no pull request — stated where a reader would otherwise infer PR-time coverage? [Clarity, Plan §Structure Decision] — PASS: `plan.md`:523-529 and again at 725-727 (*"Do not read 'gates the publish' as PR-time coverage"*), stated at both sites (Structure Decision and the compile-arm row) where a reader would otherwise infer PR-time coverage from "gates the publish." Non-PASS: the residual stated once, distant from the site making the stronger-sounding claim.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK026 Does any requirement in this domain state a pinned digest, tag or version as a **value** where the value will move, without a re-derivation recipe? [Clarity, Gap] — PASS: no literal digest/SHA/version value that will move is written anywhere in the bundle (checked: no `sha256:` literal, no hard-coded "current" digest for "the pre-089 digest"); the capability-minimums row and `spec.md` FR-023a both explicitly decline to write a value that would rot, in favour of a re-derivation recipe or a value deferred to implementation time. Non-PASS: a literal `sha256:...` or version string written as "the pre-089 digest" with no recipe to re-derive it once it moves.
- [x] CHK027 Are `FR-020`'s regression obligation and the republish safety argument distinguished — i.e. is it clear that reasoning about an opt-in gate is not the measurement FR-020 requires? [Conflict, Spec §FR-020] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `spec.md`:911 (FR-020 itself)** — *"THIS IS A MEASUREMENT — RUN THE CELLS AND COMPARE — AND AN ARGUMENT IS NOT ONE"*, naming the specific substitution the item describes (arguing safety from the counterparty emitter activating only when `INTEROP_CP_RUN_ID` is set) and why it cannot discharge the clause: it reasons about a mechanism and runs **zero** existing cells. ⚠️ **The measurement is given a producer in the same clause** — `tasks.md` T099 — so the new MUST does not itself become an obligation with nothing behind it, which is the RC-A shape this bundle just closed twice elsewhere in this batch.
- [x] CHK028 Do the requirements name which repository each obligation lands in, at every row, so a reader never has to infer it from a path prefix? [Clarity] — PASS: `plan.md` § *Project Structure* (447, 462) names the two repositories once, with explicit `# ── PARENT repo:` / `# ── LIBRARY submodule:` headers, and every row in § *External obligations* follows that path-prefix convention consistently (`library/...` vs `phase-9-harness/...`) with no row breaking it. Non-PASS: rows mixing prefixes inconsistently, or the convention never declared, forcing a reader to infer the partition from context alone.

### SPEC-FIXED items — all ten APPLIED by the orchestrator; boxes ticked

⚠️ **Fixed by ROOT CAUSE, not item by item.** The ten collapse into four edits; applying ten separate
patches would have produced ten drifting restatements of the same three facts, which is the defect this
domain produced twice already.

- **CHK001 + CHK002 + CHK005 + CHK007 + CHK009 — `interop-matrix.yml` had no obligations row, so R-11's
  decision narrowed at the `plan.md` hop.** One new row at `plan.md`:638 (**PARENT repo**, under RC-B)
  carrying the pin **(a)**, the resolution of the pin/starve tension **(b)** — no longer deferred to a task
  as *"decide the mechanism"*, which `plan.md`'s own round-2 rule scores ABSENT — the failure direction
  **(c)**, and the consumer **enumeration recipe with its publisher-vs-consumer discriminator** **(d)**.
  `plan.md`:637 is widened to state that it is one consumer and not the whole decision; `tasks.md`:62 (T003)
  drops its hard-coded *"both"* for *"every"* plus the recipe.
- **CHK008 + CHK014 + CHK015 — the consumers' failure direction was unstated.** `spec.md`:845 (FR-016b)
  gains *an unpullable pin is a SKIP and a skip is GREEN* with the cell-actually-ran obligation attached;
  `spec.md`:1004 (FR-026) gains the reachability **condition** — deliberately a condition, not a two-file
  list — and corrects FR-026's own *"the first is the safer shape"* by saying what pin-first is and is not
  inert for. Both obligation rows repeat the condition for their own workflow.
- **CHK023 — parent-side review had a need and no mechanism.** `plan.md`:513 names the mechanism;
  `plan.md`:647 gives it a producer row under RC-B.
- **CHK027 — FR-020's obligation is a measurement.** `spec.md`:911, with `tasks.md` T099 named as the
  measurement's producer in the same clause.

⚠️ **`research.md` R-11 was deliberately NOT edited.** R-11 is the dated record of what was decided; FR-026
is where the two orderings are evaluated and is therefore where the incompleteness of *"the safer shape"*
belongs. Amending the record to match a later finding is the shape this bundle's own rules forbid.
